q: Biology is the study of living things.
e: True. Biology is the study of living things. Living things are organisms: plants, animals, fungi, and microbes.

q: Biology only deals with animals and humans.
e: False. It is not true that biology only deals with animals and humans. Biology studies all living things, including plants, fungi, and microbes.

q: Living things include plants, animals, and other organisms.
e: True. Living things include plants, animals, and other organisms. Living things are organisms: plants, animals, fungi, and microbes.

q: Biology is unimportant in daily life.
e: False. It is not true that biology is unimportant in daily life. Biology matters every day, from food production to disease control.

q: Biological advances have increased food production.
e: True. Biological advances have increased food production. Plant breeding, pest control, and other biological work have raised how much food we can grow.

q: The main branches of biology include physics and chemistry.
e: False. It is not true that the main branches of biology include physics and chemistry. Physics and chemistry are other sciences; biology's own branches include botany and zoology.

q: Metabolism includes anabolism and catabolism.
e: True. Metabolism includes anabolism and catabolism. Metabolism is anabolism plus catabolism: build-up and break-down reactions in a body.

q: Growth in organisms is only seen as an increase in weight.
e: False. It is not true that growth in organisms is only seen as an increase in weight. Growth is an increase in size and organisation, not merely weight.

q: Irritability refers to living things responding to stimuli.
e: True. Irritability refers to living things responding to stimuli. Living things are organisms: plants, animals, fungi, and microbes.

q: Reproduction is the production of a new generation of offspring.
e: True. Reproduction is the production of a new generation of offspring. Reproduction makes a new generation so the species can continue.

q: All living things can reproduce only sexually.
e: False. It is not true that all living things can reproduce only sexually. Many organisms reproduce asexually as well as sexually.

q: Adaptability increases the chances of survival for species.
e: True. Adaptability increases the chances of survival for species. Adaptability helps a species survive when conditions change.

q: Viruses are considered living organisms.
e: False. It is not true that viruses are considered living organisms. Viruses are not treated as true living organisms because they cannot metabolise on their own.

q: The study of plants is known as botany.
e: True. The study of plants is known as botany. Botany is the branch of biology that studies plants.

q: Microbiology is the study of large organisms.
e: False. It is not true that microbiology is the study of large organisms. Microbiology studies microscopic organisms, not large plants or animals.

q: Cells contain DNA that carries biological information.
e: True. Cells contain DNA that carries biological information. The cell is the basic unit of structure and function in living organisms.

q: All living things are unicellular.
e: False. It is not true that all living things are unicellular. Many living things are multicellular, including plants and animals.

q: Taxonomy is the science of classification of organisms.
e: True. Taxonomy is the science of classification of organisms. Classification groups organisms by shared features so we can name and compare them.

q: Only animals are classified into kingdoms.
e: False. It is not true that only animals are classified into kingdoms. Plants, fungi, protists, and bacteria are classified into kingdoms too.

q: Eukarya includes organisms with prokaryotic cells.
e: False. It is not true that eukarya includes organisms with prokaryotic cells. Eukarya is for nucleated cells; prokaryotes belong to Bacteria or Archaea.

q: Biodiversity refers to the variety of life in the world.
e: True. Biodiversity refers to the variety of life in the world. Biodiversity is the variety of living things in an area or on Earth.

q: All organisms in the kingdom Animalia are autotrophic.
e: False. It is not true that all organisms in the kingdom Animalia are autotrophic. Animals are heterotrophic; they cannot photosynthesize.

q: Taxonomy is essential for biology because it organizes living things into categories.
e: True. Taxonomy is essential for biology because it organizes living things into categories. Living things are organisms: plants, animals, fungi, and microbes.

q: Diversity of organisms is not important in biology.
e: False. It is not true that diversity of organisms is not important in biology. Diversity is central in biology because it is how we compare and conserve life.

q: Taxonomy allows for easier study of millions of organisms.
e: True. Taxonomy allows for easier study of millions of organisms. Taxonomy sorts living things into ranked groups so millions of species can be studied.

q: There are only two kingdoms in biological classification.
e: False. It is not true that there are only two kingdoms in biological classification. Modern schemes use more than two kingdoms, commonly five or six.

q: The hierarchical system of classification includes domains, kingdoms, and species.
e: True. The hierarchical system of classification includes domains, kingdoms, and species. Classification groups organisms by shared features so we can name and compare them.

q: Taxonomic hierarchy is fixed and does not change.
e: False. It is not true that taxonomic hierarchy is fixed and does not change. Taxonomy is revised when new evidence appears.

q: Linnaeus introduced the Binomial System of Nomenclature.
e: True. Linnaeus introduced the Binomial System of Nomenclature. A binomial name has two parts: genus then species, and it is written in italics in print.

q: The first name in a binomial nomenclature is always lowercase.
e: False. It is not true that the first name in a binomial nomenclature is always lowercase. The genus name starts with a capital letter.

q: Taxonomy helps in examining the evolutionary history of organisms.
e: True. Taxonomy helps in examining the evolutionary history of organisms. Taxonomy sorts living things into ranked groups so millions of species can be studied.

q: All organisms are classified into the same kingdom regardless of their characteristics.
e: False. It is not true that all organisms are classified into the same kingdom regardless of their characteristics. Organisms go into kingdoms according to their characteristics.

q: The kingdom Fungi includes organisms that can photosynthesize.
e: False. It is not true that the kingdom Fungi includes organisms that can photosynthesize. Fungi do not photosynthesize.

q: The classification system is based on observable characteristics of organisms.
e: True. The classification system is based on observable characteristics of organisms. Classification groups organisms by shared features so we can name and compare them.

q: Taxonomy does not consider evolutionary relationships.
e: False. It is not true that taxonomy does not consider evolutionary relationships. Modern taxonomy does use evolutionary relationships.

q: The classification of organisms is important for scientific communication.
e: True. The classification of organisms is important for scientific communication. Classification groups organisms by shared features so we can name and compare them.

q: In taxonomy, similar species are grouped into different genera.
e: False. It is not true that in taxonomy, similar species are grouped into different genera. Similar species are grouped into the same genus.

q: The study of biodiversity is part of taxonomy.
e: True. The study of biodiversity is part of taxonomy. Biodiversity is the variety of living things in an area or on Earth.

q: Taxonomy is only concerned with living organisms.
e: False. It is not true that taxonomy is only concerned with living organisms. Taxonomy also names extinct organisms from fossils.

q: The classification system is static and does not adapt to new findings.
e: False. It is not true that the classification system is static and does not adapt to new findings. Classification changes as new findings arrive.

q: Taxonomy helps in identifying and naming new species.
e: True. Taxonomy helps in identifying and naming new species. Taxonomy sorts living things into ranked groups so millions of species can be studied.

q: All organisms in the kingdom Plantae are unicellular.
e: False. It is not true that all organisms in the kingdom Plantae are unicellular. Typical plants in Plantae are multicellular.

q: The kingdom Animalia includes both vertebrates and invertebrates.
e: True. The kingdom Animalia includes both vertebrates and invertebrates. Animalia covers multicellular heterotrophs that usually move and lack cell walls.

q: Taxonomy only applies to animals and not to plants or fungi.
e: False. It is not true that taxonomy only applies to animals and not to plants or fungi. Taxonomy applies to plants, fungi, and microbes as well.

q: A kingdom is a subdivision of a domain.
e: True. A kingdom is a subdivision of a domain. Domains sit above kingdoms: Bacteria, Archaea, and Eukarya.

q: There are five kingdoms of living things.
e: False. It is not true that there are five kingdoms of living things. Many courses now use six kingdoms by splitting the bacteria.

q: Archaebacteria and Eubacteria are both prokaryotic kingdoms.
e: True. Archaebacteria and Eubacteria are both prokaryotic kingdoms. Prokaryotic cells have no nucleus; their DNA sits in the cytoplasm.

q: Eukarya includes only unicellular organisms.
e: False. It is not true that eukarya includes only unicellular organisms. Eukarya includes large multicellular plants and animals as well.

q: Viruses are included in the six kingdoms of living organisms.
e: False. It is not true that viruses are included in the six kingdoms of living organisms. Viruses are not members of the living kingdoms.

q: Fungi can be unicellular or multicellular.
e: True. Fungi can be unicellular or multicellular. A multicellular organism is made of many cells that share the work of life.

q: Plants are classified under the kingdom Animalia.
e: False. It is not true that plants are classified under the kingdom Animalia. Plants belong to Plantae, not Animalia.

q: Animalia includes multicellular organisms that are heterotrophic.
e: True. Animalia includes multicellular organisms that are heterotrophic. Heterotrophs must take in food made by other organisms.

q: Eubacteria are known for their complex cellular structure.
e: False. It is not true that eubacteria are known for their complex cellular structure. Eubacteria are prokaryotes with a simple cell plan and no nucleus.

q: The kingdom Protista contains unicellular and colonial groups.
e: True. The kingdom Protista contains unicellular and colonial groups. A unicellular organism is a whole living thing made of one cell.

q: All organisms in the kingdom Fungi can photosynthesize.
e: False. It is not true that all organisms in the kingdom Fungi can photosynthesize. Not all organisms in the kingdom Fungi can photosynthesize.

q: The kingdom Plantae consists of eukaryotic organisms.
e: True. The kingdom Plantae consists of eukaryotic organisms. Plantae contains photosynthetic organisms with cellulose walls and chlorophyll.

q: The characteristics of the kingdoms are the same for all.
e: False. It is not true that the characteristics of the kingdoms are the same for all. Each kingdom is defined by its own set of traits.

q: Viruses can reproduce independently outside of host cells.
e: False. It is not true that viruses can reproduce independently outside of host cells. Viruses reproduce only inside a host cell.

q: The kingdom Animalia includes organisms that are autotrophic.
e: False. It is not true that the kingdom Animalia includes organisms that are autotrophic. The kingdom Animalia includes organisms that are not autotrophic.

q: The kingdom Protista includes both autotrophs and heterotrophs.
e: True. The kingdom Protista includes both autotrophs and heterotrophs. That is how this part of the lesson is stated.

q: All organisms in the kingdom Plantae are multicellular.
e: False. It is not true that all organisms in the kingdom Plantae are multicellular. Not all organisms in the kingdom Plantae are multicellular.

q: The kingdom Fungi is characterized by the presence of chlorophyll.
e: False. It is not true that the kingdom Fungi is characterized by the presence of chlorophyll. The kingdom Fungi is not characterized by the presence of chlorophyll.

q: Eubacteria can reproduce asexually by fission.
e: True. Eubacteria can reproduce asexually by fission. Eubacteria are prokaryotes with a relatively simple cell structure.

q: The classification of organisms is fixed and does not change over time.
e: False. It is not true that the classification of organisms is fixed and does not change over time. The classification of organisms is revised when new evidence appears over time.

q: Viruses are classified within the kingdoms of living organisms.
e: False. It is not true that viruses are classified within the kingdoms of living organisms. Viruses are not classified within the kingdoms of living organisms.
